title: Last-iterate Convergence of ADMM on Multi-affine Quadratic Equality Constrained Problem
claim: The target problem arises in diverse robotic systems where contact forces and motion variables must be jointly planned.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, photos with overlaid force and rotation annotations
description: Two side-by-side real photographs, both faded or washed out so the overlaid annotations stand out. The left panel shows the white quadruped robot Solo standing on a flat surface. Black arrows labeled f1 to f4 point at the four feet, which marks the contact forces. Above the body, a curved arrow labeled k circles a dot labeled c, which denotes a rotation about the center of mass. The right panel shows the Trifinger manipulation robot, with three white robotic fingers around a colored cube in a circular arena. Arrows f1 and f2 point at the cube's contact points, and a curved arrow k circles a dot c on the cube. The same notation in both panels shows that the two settings share one structure. The eye goes first to the robots, then to the black arrows and labels.
caption: Examples of locomotion and manipulation settings, (left) Solo [ref] and (right) Trifinger [ref]
abstract: In this paper, we study a class of non-convex optimization problems known as multi-affine quadratic equality constrained problems, which appear in various applications--from generating feasible force trajectories in robotic locomotion and manipulation to training neural networks. Although these problems are generally non-convex, they exhibit convexity or related properties when all variables except one are fixed. Under mild assumptions, we prove that the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) converges when applied to this class of problems. Furthermore, when the "degree" of non-convexity in the constraints remains within certain bounds, we show that ADMM achieves a linear convergence rate. We validate our theoretical results through practical examples in robotic locomotion.
